newsitem.title: DENMARK: Novo Nordisk poised for bumper 1997.
newsitem.headline: Novo Nordisk poised for bumper 1997.

text.p: Danish pharmaceuticals and biotechnology group Novo Nordisk A/S on Wednesday posted bumper 1996 pre-tax results, 17 percent up on the previous year, and said it saw solid progress continuing in 1997.
"Novo Nordisk expects its operations to continue to develop favourably in 1997," the firm, one of the world's leading producers of insulin and industrial enzymes, said.
It said in a statement it expected to achieve 15 percent higher operating and pre-tax profits in 1997 conditional on international currency and securities markets.
Novo Nordisk posted a 1996 pre-tax profit of 2.521 billion crowns ($386.7 million), 17 percent up on the previous year on eight percent higher consolidated turnover of 14.873 billion crowns.
The operating result increased 15 percent to 2.386 billion crowns, with net profits 15 percent up at 1.799 billion crowns.
The results were more or less in line with average forecasts and pleased analysts.
"The result is very impressive," one analyst, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

"If you adjust for costs and restructuring," Novo Nordisk's operating profits last year would have climbed by 20 percent," and even more if you take other factors such as discounts into consideration," he added.
Novo Nordisk said sales for its key Health Care and Enzyme divisions rose 12 and 11 percent respectively on the previous year, a factor which also impressed the market.

Under health care, sales of diabetes care products climbed 15 percent, with progress attributed to increased turnover in Novo Nordisk's Penfill, NovoPen and NovoLet insulin pens, notably in the United States and Asia.

It said enzyme business sales were bolstered by increased sales of detergent enzymes, which grew marginally more than those of enzymes for the process industries, with rising demand noted in Japan, Brazil and European markets.
Novo Nordisk said that it expected a positive development in business this year due to improved product mixes and increased volume.

"Increased productivity and efficiency in all our areas of operational activity will limit the increase in costs. The growth in Novo Nordisk's combined costs is anticipated to be inferior to sales growth in 1997," it said.
The Novo Nordisk share shot up 15 crowns to 705 on the announcement of its 1996 result, falling back in mid-afternoon to around 690 crowns.
The group proposed a rise in the dividend by 50 percent to 3.75 crowns per ten crown share from 2.50 crowns. ($ = 6.52 Danish Crowns) --Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
